title: Combining Parameterized Pulses and Contextual Subspace for More Practical VQE
problem: Traditional CNOT-based quantum circuits limit access to certain Hilbert space regions, and computing complete Hamiltonians via VQE requires many qubits and measurements. Scaling VQE to simulate larger molecular systems is impractical with current approaches.
motivation: Reducing quantum resource requirements makes VQE viable for simulating larger molecular structures on near-term quantum devices.
method: SpacePulse integrates parameterized quantum pulses with the contextual subspace method to enable flexible quantum operations beyond gate-based decomposition. Parameterized pulses access previously inaccessible Hilbert space regions. The contextual subspace method computes corrections using fewer qubits and measurements than full VQE. A Pauli grouping strategy optimizes measurement efficiency.
key_novelty: Combining parameterized quantum pulses with contextual subspace approximation to substantially reduce quantum resource costs while maintaining solution quality.
contributions: SpacePulse framework integrating parameterized pulses and contextual subspace methods
Demonstrated reduction in required qubits and measurements compared to traditional VQE
Pauli grouping strategy for optimizing measurement overhead
Enhanced scalability for molecular structure simulation with reduced quantum resources
